sections.voiceover: In 1897, performer Harry Houdini began documenting his grueling dime museum career. Collector Dr. Bruce Averbook preserved this rare two-year record through 1899. What hidden reality did this red pocket diary reveal about Houdini?
sections.visual_cue: Historical photos of 1890s dime museum storefronts and traveling circus tents.
sections.sfx_cue: Faint crowd chatter from historic audio archive
b_roll: Historical archival photograph of 1890s dime museum hall
Vintage photograph of turn-of-the-century circus encampment

sections.voiceover: But he wasn't alone, as his wife Bess drove their crucial survival during those grueling shows.
sections.visual_cue: Historical portrait of Bess Houdini alongside early stage apparatus.
b_roll: Archival publicity portrait of Bess and Harry Houdini

sections.voiceover: National Geographic writer Nina Strochlic detailed how Bess shaped his international stardom. They weathered brutal medicine shows and circuses together across early vaudeville. Averbook published these genuine entries spanning 1897 to 1899 in a new book.
sections.visual_cue: Page flip transition showing published book pages alongside historic vaudeville playbills.
sections.sfx_cue: Camera shutter click followed by quiet riser
b_roll: Early vaudeville theatre stage historical photography
Published book pages from Escaping Obscurity

sections.voiceover: That small red diary captured Houdini's true rise from 1897.
